title: Comparatives and superlatives
point: Compare two things with -er or more ... than, pick out one of a group with the -est or the most, and show equality with as ... as.

sentences.ja: 電車で行ったほうがバスより早いよ。
sentences.text: The train's faster than the bus.
sentences.note: English compares the two things directly instead of saying "it's better to go by".

sentences.ja: 今日は昨日よりだいぶ寒いね。
sentences.text: It's a lot colder today than yesterday.
sentences.note: Use "a lot" or "much" before a comparative, never "very".

sentences.ja: このカフェ、この辺で一番おいしいコーヒー出すんだよ。
sentences.text: This cafe makes the best coffee around here.

sentences.ja: 思ってたほど難しくなかった。
sentences.text: It wasn't as hard as I expected.

sentences.ja: 弟は僕と同じくらいの背の高さです。
sentences.text: My brother is about as tall as I am.

sentences.ja: できるだけ早く返信します。
sentences.text: I'll get back to you as soon as I can.

sentences.ja: もう少し安いのはありますか？
sentences.text: Do you have anything a bit cheaper?
sentences.note: "Anything cheaper" is the natural shop phrase; "cheaper one" needs a clear noun.

sentences.ja: この授業は今学期で一番面白い。
sentences.text: This is the most interesting class I'm taking this semester.

sentences.ja: 前回の実験結果のほうがずっと信頼できる。
sentences.text: The results from the last experiment are far more reliable.

sentences.ja: 人生で一番大変な一週間だった。
sentences.text: That was the toughest week of my life.
